transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-04-14 14:00 UTC | Duration: ~62m | Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Alyssa (CISO, HeliosGrid), Tom (Cloud Eng), Priya (Sec Ops), Evan (Procurement)

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, appreciate you carving out the time. quick intros, I'm Jordan, I'm the AE on the account. Maya's our solutions engineer, she'll cover the KMS and logs stuff.
[00:06] Alyssa: Thanks, Jordan. Alyssa here, CISO at HeliosGrid. I'm joined by Tom, who's our cloud lead, and Priya from SecOps. Evan's on for procurement items.
[00:12] Jordan: Great. Goal for today is a posture review — SOC 2 / ISO — and to make sure you have the artifacts and map of controls you need for your audit and regulatory constraints. Also cover RBAC/SSO and KMS questions. Sound right?
[00:19] Priya: Yep, especially around audit logs retention and how we can export evidence for auditors.
[00:23] Maya: I'll demonstrate the Trust Center briefly and then dig into key management flows. Heads up, I'll call out a couple of places where our auto-generated names get munged — sometimes the transcript will show K V cache instead of KV cache, etc — sorry in advance for that.
[00:34] Tom: One ask up front — we require EU residency for a subset of training data / logs. We'll outline the regions later.
[00:39] Jordan: Noted. Okay we'll run through the SOC 2 artifacts first.

--- Summary / Artifacts ---
[00:45] Jordan: Redwood maintains a SOC 2 Type II — the report covers our control environment for the period Oct 2025–Mar 2026. We can provide the full PDF under NDA; we also surface a condensed controls mapping in the Trust Center.
[01:00] Alyssa: For auditors, do we get raw evidence? e.g., logs, change management tickets?
[01:05] Maya: We provide a couple of mechanisms: 1) read-only Trust Center access so you can view reports and mapped controls and 2) for auditor requests we can produce evidence packages — screenshots, logs extracts, config snapshots — typically on a per-request basis. There's an evidence export workflow.
[01:18] Alyssa: Is that automated or ad hoc? We prefer a reproducible path for recurring audits.
[01:22] Maya: There's an export feature that we can schedule; it isn't fully push-button for every customer yet but we do have standard packages we ship. For enterprise customers we can automate exports to an S3 bucket or to your SIEM.
[01:35] Tom: S3 transfer would be ideal. What's the retention window for audit logs on your side?
[01:40] Maya: By default, platform logs are retained 90 days in the Trust Center. For Dedicated / Private deployments we can extend retention or forward logs to your account for long-term storage. We can also offer event-based offload to your S3 with lifecycle rules.

--- RBAC / SSO ---
[02:05] Jordan: On RBAC and SSO: we support SAML 2.0 for SSO, SCIM for user provisioning, and role-based permissions in the console. You can map SCIM groups to roles (admin, observer, auditor).
[02:17] Priya: How granular are the roles? Can we restrict token creation per team or per environment?
[02:22] Maya: Yes, roles are scoped — you can restrict API key creation to specific teams, and separate model access scopes so only certain service accounts can call production endpoints. There are a few built-in roles but you can also create custom roles for more precise permissions.
[02:35] Tom: Does SCIM support group sync from our directory with nested groups? We've had pain there before.
[02:40] Maya: SCIM supports groups and attributes; nested groups sometimes need mapping on the IdP side. We usually recommend flattening group mappings for SCIM. We can share an example mapping for Okta and Azure AD.

--- KMS / Encryption ---
[03:10] Maya: On encryption and KMS: two main patterns — Redwood-managed keys (default) and customer-managed keys (CMK) via KMS. With CMK, you can bring your own key in AWS KMS or GCP KMS, and for Private deployments we support HSM-backed keys.
[03:26] Alyssa: We require HSM-backed keys for certain workloads. Is that supported in the hosted model?
[03:30] Maya: Hosted can support customer-managed keys using cloud KMS — those are HSM-backed by the cloud providers. For isolated on-prem or private VPC deployments we can integrate with your HSM directly or through a partner HSM gateway.
[03:44] Tom: Key rotation — can we rotate keys without a full outage, and what about the token cache / KV cache implications?
[03:50] Maya: Key rotation is supported in a rolling fashion. For long-lived encryption materials (e.g., model artifacts), rotation is handled by envelope encryption so you rotate data keys without re-encrypting the whole store. For runtime tokens there's a short TTL; we keep the KV cache separate and rotation is transparent to active requests. There are edge cases we should test during the workshop.
[04:08] Alyssa: Is there audit logging for key usage? We need per-request key usage logs for our auditors.
[04:13] Maya: Yes — we surface key usage events (kid used, operation, timestamp) and can forward KMS logs (CloudTrail / Audit Logs) to your aggregator. We need to remove any PII from exported logs by default, but we can include request metadata for traceability.

--- Data residency & deployment options ---
[04:40] Jordan: You've flagged EU residency. Quick overview: hosted nodes in eu-west-1 are available; Dedicated provides pinned capacity in a region; Private gives you full control on-prem or in your VPC. Which model are you leaning to?
[04:52] Tom: We prefer hosted to start but need EU-only residency for some datasets — ideally data-processing in eu-west only.
[04:58] Maya: That's doable. We can pin routing for those tenant IDs to eu-west; we also can configure regional model variants. We'll need to see your allowed regions list to validate no cross-region fallbacks.
[05:10] Alyssa: Also need to know about backups and where snapshots land. Are backups geo-located to us?
[05:16] Maya: Backups for hosted are regional but some orchestration metadata may be in the control plane (which is multi-region). For strict residency we recommend Dedicated or Private so both runtime and snapshots stay in your VPC/region. We'll capture the exact backup flows in the follow-up doc.

--- Evidence & Controls mapping ---
[05:45] Jordan: On controls mapping, we have a pre-built matrix that maps Redwood controls to SOC 2 Trust Services Criteria and ISO 27001 Annex A. We'll share that matrix — it shows the control owner, evidence type, and sample artifacts.
[05:57] Alyssa: Will that matrix include evidence locations? e.g., where in Trust Center to find config snapshots, or links to CloudTrail exports?
[06:02] Jordan: Yes, the matrix includes pointers and example artifacts. For security-sensitive items we provide redacted examples but the full evidence can be produced under an NDA or via the auditor request flow.

--- Procurement & contract questions (brief) ---
[06:28] Evan: From procurement: if we go Dedicated what's the typical contract length and SLA for data residency? Also, can we add an addendum for audit support?
[06:35] Jordan: Dedicated has reserved capacity commitments — typical terms are 12–36 months depending on scale. SLA addenda and audit support add-ons are negotiable at the enterprise tier. We can pull legal and review a draft SOW.

--- Clarifications and small corrections (transcription artefacts) ---
[07:00] Maya: Small note — sometimes our internal names like "Trust Center" show up as "trust portal" in exports; apologies if the transcript is inconsistent. Also we might mention KV cache as K V cash in the transcript.

--- Q&A and edge cases ---
[07:15] Priya: If an auditor requests a live readout of controls, can your team join and provide commentary?
[07:20] Jordan: Yes, we offer auditor liaisons for enterprise customers — typically SE joins for 1–2 hours to explain artefacts. We'll include that as an option in the next steps.
[07:28] Tom: About log delivery: what formats and schemas do you support for log export? JSON events? Syslog?
[07:34] Maya: We can export JSON events to S3, forward via syslog to an endpoint, or stream via partners like Datadog / Splunk. We also provide CSV extracts for certain evidence types.
[07:44] Alyssa: Is there a cost for longer retention?
[07:47] Jordan: For hosted, yes there is an add-on to extend retention beyond default. For Dedicated/Private it's generally a part of the deployment cost or negotiated separately. We'll include pricing ranges.

--- Recap and explicit next steps ---
[08:10] Jordan: Quick recap: we'll share the SOC 2 Type II report and the controls matrix, grant Trust Center read-only access for Alyssa and her audit team, Maya will produce the KMS/key flow doc, and we'll schedule a technical deep dive for KMS + private deployment.
[08:23] Alyssa: Sounds good. Two asks — one: give us an example of an evidence export package; two: confirm the S3 transfer workflow for daily log offload.
[08:31] Maya: We'll attach a sample export and a step-by-step S3 setup.
[08:34] Evan: From procurement, please include the rough Dedicated pricing band and SLA addendum template for review.
[08:38] Jordan: Got it. We'll get the SOC report and the Trust Center link over by Friday.

[08:50] Maya: One final technical note — if you use CMKs in AWS, CloudTrail will show KMS:Decrypt/Encrypt calls. We can surface those in the Trust Center events with request IDs so it's traceable back to requests.
[08:59] Tom: Great. We'll provide a list of our regions and the workloads that require EU-only handling.

[09:10] Jordan: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the packet and schedule the workshop for week of 4/27. If anything else pops up, shoot an email or ping me directly.
[09:18] Alyssa: Thank you. Appreciate the clarity.
[09:21] Jordan: Thanks, bye.

End of transcript.
